narrative.human_title: Pokemon Valley: when the card becomes a place
narrative.why_it_matters: Pokemon Valley is a beautiful little refusal of the usual chase-card logic. There is no Charizard, no mascot close-up, no little attack math to obsess over. Instead, Bessatsu CoroCoro hands the reader a jumbo Stadium: a Pokemon place large enough to feel like a poster, a magazine insert that says the world itself is collectible. Naoyo Kimura matters here because the card is environmental. The agent has to keep that physical and narrative scale intact: jumbo, Stadium, Bessatsu route, source index 109, and valley-as-place before the word 'promo' flattens it.

narrative.human_title: Pokemon Valley 109: a landscape too large for the pocket
narrative.why_it_matters: Pokemon Valley feels like a card stretching toward a poster. It is a Stadium, but also a scene; a promo, but also a place; a magazine insert, but also a tiny map of the world Pokémon was building around its creatures. That is why the jumbo format matters. If an agent sees only the name, it misses the whole object. The scale, Bessatsu route, Stadium identity, and Kimura environmental art are what make this row breathe.
